title: Oil Surge Drags Nasdaq Lower While Super Micro Rallies on Margin Surprise
excerpt: Rising crude prices and U.S.-Iran tensions weighed on Wall Street Wednesday, but AI server maker Super Micro Computer surged nearly 20% after doubling its gross margin forecast and reporting a record $60 billion backlog.
body:
• The Nasdaq composite fell 0.6% as crude oil prices climbed more than 2%, with Brent crude topping $94 per barrel amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict.
  • Super Micro Computer surged nearly 20% — the S&P 500's top gainer — after doubling its fiscal Q4 gross margin guidance to 15%-17% and reporting over $60 billion in new orders.
  • Nvidia gained 3% to lead the Dow, while Alphabet and Tesla reported earnings after the close.
  • Indian benchmarks fell for a third straight session, with the Nifty 50 down 0.79% and the Sensex off 0.92%, as higher oil prices stoked inflation fears for the world's third-largest crude importer.

Oil Headwinds Cap a Mixed Session

Wall Street closed lower on Wednesday as a fresh surge in oil prices overshadowed a string of positive earnings reports. The Dow Jones Industrial Average eked out a six-point decline, the S&P 500 shed 0.1%, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite dropped 0.6%, remaining below its 21-day exponential moving average. Small caps fared worse, with the Russell 2000 losing 0.9%.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures jumped more than 2% to around $86.40 per barrel, while the global benchmark Brent crude rose to $94.90 — its highest since June 11 — as the U.S.-Iran confrontation continued to disrupt critical energy chokepoints. Two Saudi oil tankers reversed course in the Red Sea on Tuesday, and a tanker was struck in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Reuters.

The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.66%, nearing 2026 highs, while Bitcoin sank to around $65,900.

Super Micro's Margin Surprise Lifts AI Trade

The day's standout story was Super Micro Computer, which surged nearly 20% to become the S&P 500's biggest gainer. The AI server maker disclosed Tuesday evening that its fiscal fourth-quarter gross margins are expected to land between 15% and 17% — roughly double the 8.2% to 8.4% the company had previously guided.

"We believe SMCI likely was able to take advantage of scarcity to more favorably price products and/or shift customers to a richer mix of servers."

— Matt Bryson, Analyst, Wedbush Securities

Super Micro also revealed that it received more than $60 billion in new orders during the quarter, pushing its backlog to a record. Revenue is expected near the low end of its $11 billion to $12.5 billion guidance, but the margin improvement and order surge overshadowed that softer top-line number. The company, which counts SpaceX among its major AI customers, reports official fourth-quarter results on August 11.

The rally rippled across the server and chip ecosystem. Dell Technologies rose 9.3%, Hewlett Packard Enterprise gained 3%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index added 0.9%. Nvidia climbed 3% to lead the Dow, reclaiming its 50-day moving average and extending its winning streak to three sessions.

Earnings Bonanza Keeps Markets on Edge

Wednesday marked one of the busiest days of the current earnings season. AT&T jumped 3.5% after topping second-quarter earnings estimates, while transportation equipment maker Wabtec surged 11% on strong results. On the losing side, GE Vernova sank 7% after missing profit forecasts, and TE Connectivity dropped 8% despite beating expectations.

The main event, though, was after the bell. Alphabet reported a 24% increase in second-quarter revenue, but its free cash flow turned negative. Tesla's free cash flow also fell as it booked $5.8 billion in capital expenditures. IBM and ServiceNow were also set to report, making this a pivotal evening for tech sentiment heading into Thursday's session.

Indian Markets Buckle Under Oil Pressure

The oil-driven anxiety hit Indian markets harder. The benchmark Nifty 50 fell 0.79% to 23,996.25, while the BSE Sensex shed 0.92% to 76,755.05, marking a third consecutive session of losses, according to Reuters. Fourteen of 16 major sectors posted declines, with IT stocks dropping 1.5% and financials losing 1.3%.

"While the ongoing earnings season has largely been in line with expectations, the broader challenges are creating an overhang for markets."

— Pankaj Pandey, Head of Retail Research, ICICI Securities

For Indian-origin investors and the diaspora with exposure to both U.S. and Indian equities, the session underscored a familiar dilemma: what boosts American energy stocks pressures India's import-heavy economy. As the world's third-largest crude importer, India faces widening trade deficits and corporate margin compression when oil spikes. Pharma stocks added to the pain, falling 1.3% after President Trump outlined a phased tariff plan targeting imported generic medicines — a sector where Indian firms dominate global supply.

What's Next

Markets now pivot to digesting after-hours results from Alphabet and Tesla, two Magnificent Seven members whose guidance could set the tone for the rest of earnings season. The oil picture remains volatile: Brent crude has surged from $76 on July 10 to nearly $95, and any further escalation in the Strait of Hormuz could push prices even higher. For Indian markets, all eyes are on whether crude breaches the psychologically important $100 mark, which would intensify pressure on the Reserve Bank of India's inflation calculus and potentially delay rate cuts that investors have been pricing in.
